context.alert_text: Payments dead-letter queue receiving messages while the consumer reports errors

root_cause.hypothesis: The 07:33 deploy (version 15, previous 14) introduced a code change that fails to validate/parse incoming message fields (type mismatch: expecting string, receiving int), causing almost all invocations to error out and messages to be dead-lettered, filling the DLQ.
evidence: D1: version=15, previous=14, previous_basis=served live traffic before this version
ruled_out: Throttling: M6 lambda_throttles=0 rules out concurrency exhaustion
Timeout: M8 lambda_duration_max_ms=88.2 is far below M1 lambda_timeout_s=30, ruling out timeout-driven failures
DLQ-side change: C5 shows no change on the DLQ itself

citations.quote: previous_basis=served live traffic before this version

proposal.reasoning: The new version (15) deployed at 07:33:38 correlates directly with a surge of ValidationError/type-mismatch failures (388 errors of 402 invocations) and a growing DLQ. Rolling back the Lambda alias to the previous version (14), which served live traffic successfully before this deploy, should stop the error cascade and halt further DLQ growth.
proposal.expected_effect: Lambda resumes processing messages successfully as it did on version 14, error rate drops near zero, and the DLQ stops filling (though existing 286 messages will still need a redrive after the rollback is confirmed stable).

reasons: Passed all policies. Held for operator approval before execution.
